genetic_context.description: DOMINANT_NEGATIVE rather than LOSS_OF_FUNCTION on three converging grounds: every reported disease allele is missense and none is truncating, the cell-biology literature shows that mutant DHX16 added to wild-type nuclear extract actively inhibits splicing rather than merely failing to support it, and one residue is hit by two different substitutions. It is an inference from allele spectrum and from non-patient constructs, not a measurement on a patient allele in a patient cell, and is flagged as such in `discussions`.

nodes.description: DHX16 is the human Prp2 orthologue and acts after the pre-catalytic B complex has assembled, converting it to a catalytically competent spliceosome. A defective DHX16 therefore does not block spliceosome assembly - the B complex still forms - it blocks the transition to catalysis. This is a precise step-level lesion, and it is why the disease is a spliceosomopathy of activation rather than of assembly.

nodes.description: Affected transcripts retain introns and accumulate in the nucleus rather than being degraded by nonsense-mediated decay - which matters, because it means the cell neither makes the protein nor clears the failed message. Only a subset of intron-containing genes is affected in the dominant-negative experiments, and in the one assay performed on an actual patient allele the affected transcripts were HSPH1 and FOS. Which transcripts are sensitive, and why, is not known.

nodes.description:
A node for the fact that a universal splicing defect produces a selective phenotype. Retina, cochlea, skeletal muscle and the developing CNS are consistently affected; most other tissues are not. This is not an oddity of this disease alone - it is the central puzzle of the spliceosomopathies as a class, where core spliceosome components produce retinitis pigmentosa or craniofacial disease rather than global collapse.
Nothing curated here explains it, and the node exists to hold the gap rather than to assert a mechanism. Candidate explanations in the wider field - tissue differences in splicing-factor abundance, in transcript intron burden, or in the reserve capacity of the spliceosome - are not tested in DHX16 and are not asserted.
